A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FindingDory with the same authors, benchmark design, and task suite. Text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated-agent evaluations, supervised fine-tuning results, frame-subsampling experiments, and navigation failure analyses in Figures 2–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds GLM evaluation, subsampling-solvability results, and original VSI-Bench transfer experiments.

M1.justification: The original benchmark construction and hierarchical agents remain. Beyond v1's goal-index supervised fine-tuning, v2 adds an oracle-conditioned reasoning-trace generation, rephrasing, and filtering pipeline, plus GRPO co-training with a custom goal-frame precision reward (Appendices B.5 and F). These substantially extend the training procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds Video-R1-CoT-165k and Video-R1-260k training data and evaluates transfer to real-world egocentric video reasoning on VSI-Bench, including multiple-choice and numerical questions. This extends coverage beyond the retained simulated embodied-navigation tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds GLM-4.1V-Thinking to the existing FindingDory comparison (Figure 2 and Table 4). The new transfer comparison also introduces zero-shot, Video-R1-only SFT, and Video-R1-only GRPO controls against FindingDory-augmented training (Table 3), substantially broadening the comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces protocols for 2,490 multiple-choice and 2,640 numerical questions, with 48-frame SFT training/inference and 32-frame GRPO training with 64-frame inference, distinct budgets, and checkpoint selection rules. Separately, the main-text training count changes from 82,174 to 79,213, while v2 Appendices B.1 and D.5 retain 82,174; the actual dataset-size change is unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled comparisons with and without FindingDory training to investigate transfer, alongside mixing-ratio and frame-count sensitivity findings in Appendix F. Appendix B.4 explicitly tests whether 96-frame subsampling removes valid goal frames. The original frame-count, navigation-error, sanity-check, and qualitative analyses are retained, although some move.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed estimates, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests, or comparable uncertainty measures. The new results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing Figure 2 scores are retained; GLM's 23.49% overall success is added. New Table 3 reports SFT MCQ accuracy of 35.06 with FindingDory versus 33.33 without it, but numerical accuracy of 32.35 versus 32.67. GRPO reports 35.42/34.82 versus 33.57/33.90 for MCQ/numerical accuracy. These are newly evaluated training conditions, absent from v1. Appendix B.4 also adds approximately 1% solvability loss after subsampling.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds a formal reward definition: zero for mismatched subgoal counts, otherwise the fraction of predicted frames belonging to their reference sets. Existing success and SPL definitions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a procedurally extensible 60-task embodied-memory benchmark, hierarchical VLM/navigation evaluations, and diagnostic efficiency metrics. The three introduction contribution statements retain their meaning. Explicitly mentioning fine-tuned open-source models in v2's abstract highlights an approach already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 corrects the SC-SR/DTG-SR interpretation in Section 5, distinguishing distant-but-visible receptacles from nearby targets. Appendix B.4 newly explains that retaining a valid goal frame does not preserve the context needed to select it. The transfer results receive a sim-to-real interpretation. Appendix A's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B.5 and F provide substantial new reproducibility information: DeepSeek-based trace-generation and rephrasing prompts, filtering rules yielding 72,973 labeled samples, data mixtures, frame budgets, hardware, optimization settings, and checkpoint selection. These document the added training pipelines; the PDFs do not establish newly released code or data.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Video-R1, DeepSeek-R1, GLM-4.1V-Thinking, and vLLM/PagedAttention, while removing explicit ABO, Google Scanned Objects, and AI2-THOR references. The related-work discussion and positioning around isolating memory from exploration remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially condenses and rewrites the benchmark description, merges the overview and task subsections, reorganizes the results discussion, shortens the conclusion, and moves sanity checks into Appendix B.6. These are extensive editorial and structural revisions beyond the newly added experiments.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column conference formatting, relocating and resizing figures and tables. v2 adds Tables 3–4 and Figures 6–9, updates Figure 2's series and legend, and swaps Figure 3's object/receptacle panels. Table 4 largely redisplays existing Figure 2 results, supplemented by GLM.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper with real-world transfer evidence, an explicit subsampling-solvability analysis, clearer numerical reporting, and a corrected relaxed-metric interpretation. These provide useful validation beyond v1. The gains are limited by conflicting training-set counts and an overly broad 'consistent gains' description despite Table 3's slight SFT numerical-accuracy decline. Overall, the added evidence and clarification support a limited net improvement.
